items.title: Deep Purple’s Ian Gillan Hospitalized Following Medical Emergency, Two Shows Postponed
items.summary:
Deep Purple postponed two German concerts after singer Ian Gillan was hospitalized following a medical emergency. The band announced the change in an Instagram statement on Saturday, Oct. 31, pulling that evening's show at QI Arena in Leipzig and a subsequent date at Sporthalle Hamburg.

"This comes as a result of a medical emergency involving Ian Gillan, which has resulted in his current hospitalisation," the group wrote. Billboard reported that Deep Purple offered no further detail on Gillan's condition and gave no indication of when he might leave the hospital. The statement acknowledged the timing, with the band saying it understood the announcement came at short notice and shared the disappointment of fans in both cities.

Deep Purple said it is looking for a "suitable time to reschedule" the Leipzig and Hamburg performances, and that tickets bought for the original dates will be honored at the new ones. The current lineup around Gillan includes guitarist Simon McBride, bassist Roger Glover, drummer Ian Paice and keyboardist Don Airey.

The band has been touring behind its SPLAT! world tour since late summer, with remaining dates booked across Europe, the United Kingdom, South America and Mexico through late December. Those shows have not been addressed in the band's statement beyond the two postponements.

Gillan first joined Deep Purple in 1969 and has fronted the group across multiple stints, singing on signatures including "Smoke on the Water" and "Highway Star." His hospitalization follows a difficult stretch for the band's extended family: former bassist and vocalist Glenn Hughes, who announced his retirement from touring earlier this year, underwent a 10-hour open-heart surgery and said in mid-October that he was recovering at home.

For now, the only firm information is what the band posted — two shows off the calendar, tickets still valid, and no timetable for Gillan's release or the rescheduled dates.

items.title: James Hetfield Says Turnstile Turned Down Touring with Metallica
items.summary:
James Hetfield says Metallica asked Turnstile to join them on tour and the Baltimore band declined. The Metallica frontman made the comment on a recent episode of his SiriusXM show Riff Life, as reported by Consequence.

"We wanted to get them on tour, and they said no," Hetfield said. "They're doing good on their own already." He did not say when the invitation was extended or which run of dates it concerned.

Hetfield spent the rest of the segment recommending the band rather than complaining about the rejection. "What a vibe they bring. Go see them play if you can," he said. "They sound great on their records and recordings, but if you see them live you totally get it. We've hung out with them a bit. Super cool guys, super fun. They've got a gal in the band now, which is fun."

Metallica's own touring plans are already set well into the future. The band is scheduled to begin a North American stadium tour in 2027, with Limp Bizkit opening.

Turnstile, meanwhile, has continued to headline on its own terms, which is the reason Hetfield gave for the no. Neither the band nor its representatives have responded publicly to his account of the offer.

items.title: LAPD Arrests Two for Murder of Christina Downer, Sister to ‘SNL’ Writer Jimmy Fowlie
items.summary:
The Los Angeles Police Department announced Friday that it has arrested two people in the murder of Christina Downer, the sister of Saturday Night Live writer Jimmy Fowlie. Detectives took Downer's boyfriend, Delorean Bijon Brandon, and Kaylee Nicole Markowski into custody on Thursday.

Downer was reported missing on Dec. 18, 2025, after her ex-husband requested a welfare check, having not heard from her for an extended stretch. According to police, Brandon told investigators that Downer had moved out months earlier and left behind all of her belongings, including her car and her dog.

The case moved to the department's Robbery-Homicide Division after Downer's cellphone washed ashore on Santa Monica Beach. In a statement cited by The Hollywood Reporter, police said detectives "identified Delorean Brandon and Kaylee Markowski as the individuals responsible for Downer's murder, the disposal of her body, and the concealment of their involvement."

Fowlie posted publicly about his sister's disappearance on Dec. 22, 2025, circulating several photographs of her and asking for help. In April, he wrote that "the LAPD has informed our family that Christina is no longer alive, and the case has officially transitioned from a missing person to a homicide investigation."

In that same April post, Fowlie said he believed his sister's "phone and social media were compromised" in the weeks before she vanished, and that whoever took the phone "used it to hide the fact she was gone, to ask for money, and to create a false narrative that she was going 'off the grid.'" He added: "I am sharing this because I believe that whoever is responsible is hoping to erase her in every way possible. I want to amplify her story in the only way I know how. And to express that she was a beautiful person who matters in this world, especially to me."

The Robbery-Homicide Division will present its findings to the Los Angeles County District Attorney's Office for filing consideration. Police said the investigation remains open.
